title.narrative: Guidelines for prosecutors and capacitated relevant enforcement personnel are revised in order to improve implementation and for personnel to carry out their duties in a human rights compliant manner

1) Research and recommendations published in a book on supervision in investigation and adjudication. 2)Research findings and relevant policy on how to concretely strengthen the supervision mechanisms in investigation and adjudication phases by procuratorial organs has been discussed with legislators and decision makers. 3) 1200 prosecutors from developed and less developed areas of China have been trained.

target.value: 1) Field study on supervision during the investigation and adjudication phase. 2) Two research seminars discussing the finding from the field study. 3) Two large scale trainings of prosecutors on latest amendments to the Criminal Procedure Law conducted and the outcomes thereof assessed. 4) International study visit to Norway and Denmark.

actual.value: 1) A project specific baseline based on the field research conducted in the first part of 2019 was developed (2019 target). 2) Researchers conducted field research in selected cities in eastern, central and western China. 3) Two research seminars were conducted during 2020 with a total of 80 prosecutors participating. 4) Two large scale trainings of prosecutors were held with a total of 483 prosecutors and the outcomes assessed. 5) The international study visit to Norway and Denmark did not take place since international travel became impossible due to COVID-19 restrictions.

target.value: 1) Development of project specific baseline. 2) Field study on supervision during the investigation and adjudication phase. 3) Development of training effectiveness tool. 4) Two research seminars discussing the findings from the field study. 5) Two large scale trainings of prosecutors on latest amendments to the Criminal Procedure Law. 6) Assessment of the results of the prosecutors training. 7) Recommendations on improving supervision on investigation and adjudication phase.

actual.value: 1) The field study covering 16 procuratorates across 8 provinces in China was conducted. Data and analyses used for the baseline. 2) A tool for measuring the effect of the training of prosecutors was developed and applied during trainings in 2019. 3) One large scale two-day research seminar was held in a city in Shanxi Province with close to 130 participants. Based on the discussion a research report was drafted, including a list of recommendations for further improving the procuratorial supervision mechanisms. 4) Two large scale training of prosecutors were held in 2019 in two cities in different provinces with a total of 461 participants. The trainings each lasted five days and included lectures on procuratorial organs in criminal justice and the system of guilty plea for leniency system. 5) Based on the data collected using the training effectiveness tool, two summary reports were developed providing information for further improving future trainings. 6) A list of 20 recommendations were put forward to relevant Chinese authorities of which two recommendations were eventually accepted by legislators.
No additional results for this year due to activities put on hold due to COVID-19 restrictions.

title.narrative: Increased realisation of civil, economic and social rights in China through a functioning legal system and effective access to justice for all in support of the Chinese Government’s own policy documents and reform priorities set out in the Fourth Plenum Decision and the 2015 Guidelines on Strengthening the Legal Aid System, and implementation of the National Human Rights Action Plan (2016-2020) and SDG Implementation Plan.

Accused and detainee’s rights are protected by law and in practice through improved legislation and guidelines as well as enhanced human rights knowledge and capacity of Criminal Procedure Law enforcement personnel.

target.value: 1. DIHR partners have presented research-founded proposals for legislative recommendations for human rights compliant improvements in relevant laws and policies, particularly the Criminal Law and Criminal Procedure Law. 2. Criminal Procedure Law enforcement personnel, trained by DIHR partners indicate in post-training surveys that they use the new knowledge on human rights and the Criminal Law and Criminal Procedure Law in their work.

actual.value:
Extensive field research on the implementation of the Criminal Law and Criminal Procedure Law across China carried out by partners. Meeting held to present 20 research-driven recommendations regarding the implementation Rules on the Criminal Procedure Law. Later two of these recommendations were adopted into the rules: Article 268 specifies that prosecutors shall provide a designated space for duty lawyers to meet with detainees; Article 662 allows for prosecutors to intervene when incidents of human rights violations occur in custodial settings.
1,400 prosecutors have been trained. In order to measure outcomes of training, partners implemented pre- and post-training surveys to capture self-reports. For trainings conducted by one partner institution, 95% or more of participants reported improvements in knowledge on human rights topics related to the specific training topics. More than 95% percent of participants also reported that they would implement what they learned on the various topics of discussion. The survey regarding trainings conducted by another partner institution had a low response rate, but among the responses, prosecutors did articulate take-aways from the training and plans of action for application training knowledge to work context.

title.narrative: Criminal Procedure Law (CPL) enforcement personnel have been capacitated to effectively implement the Criminal Procedure Law and carry out their duties in a human rights compliant manner

Approx. 900 prosecutors from both developed and less developed regions trained using the updated textbook and training/resource materials.
The textbook “Research on Pre-Trial Procedure” and training/resource materials reflect new national judicial interpretations of relevance to human rights compliant criminal procedures, experience from prosecutors in different parts of the country, as well as international standards and best practices.

target.value: At least three seminars with prosecutors. Assessment of the results of the prosecutors training.

actual.value: Assessment of the results of the prosecutors training in 2019 was completed, but other activities were not possible due to COVID-19 restrictions.
No additional results for this year due to activities put on hold due to COVID-19 restrictions.

target.value:
Baseline report jointly developed with partner for the purpose of identifying the main legal issues at stake within the thematic areas of the project and the challenges faced by and knowledge of prosecutors within the thematic aspects identified in the project.
Analytical and field study on pre-trial procedures in criminal law in at least 6 procuratorates at different levels in 2 different provinces.

Revise textbook, training and resource materials for prosecutors. Development of a training effectiveness tool.
At least four seminars with prosecutors.
Assessment of the results of the prosecutors training.

actual.value:
The baseline report and analytical field study (2018 targets) were finalized in 2019.
656 prosecutors were trained through 4 training courses in different provinces. The trainings were well received and besides the participating prosecutors, there were an additional 200 participants present at the trainings, including staff of procuratorial organs, judges and lawyers.
2000 copies of the revised textbook “Research on Criminal Prosecution Practices” were published and distributed to participants during trainings. The book includes eight chapters, including on topics such as reform of the litigation system and responses from prosecutors, human rights protection in criminal proceedings, evaluation of evidence, protection of rights of juvenile defendants etc.
